title: High-Performing Compute & Storage
oneLiner: Pick the right compute model and storage tier so workloads run fast and elastically.
examWeightNote: Part of Design High-Performing Architectures (24% of the exam).
objectives: Match workloads to EC2 instance families, Lambda, and containers (ECS/EKS/Fargate).
Choose the right storage: S3, EBS volume types, EFS, and instance store.
Use caching (ElastiCache, CloudFront) to reduce latency and offload backends.
Understand S3 performance and when to use S3 Transfer Acceleration or multipart uploads.

services.name: Amazon EC2 (instance families)
services.purpose: Compute optimized for general (M), compute (C), memory (R/X), storage (I/D), or accelerated (P/G) workloads.

services.name: AWS Lambda
services.purpose: Serverless, event-driven compute that scales automatically with no servers to manage.

services.name: Amazon EBS
services.purpose: Network-attached block storage; gp3/gp2 (general), io1/io2 (high IOPS), st1/sc1 (throughput/cold HDD).

services.name: Amazon EFS / FSx
services.purpose: Shared file storage; EFS is elastic NFS for Linux, FSx offers Windows/Lustre file systems.

services.name: Amazon ElastiCache
services.purpose: In-memory Redis/Memcached cache to speed up reads and offload databases.

keyConcepts: Choose the EC2 family by bottleneck: compute-optimized (C) for CPU-bound, memory-optimized (R/X) for large in-memory datasets, storage-optimized (I/D) for high local IOPS.
Use Lambda for short, event-driven, spiky workloads (no capacity planning); use containers/EC2 for long-running or specialized workloads.
EBS is single-AZ block storage attached to one instance (except Multi-Attach io2); EFS is multi-AZ shared file storage many instances can mount at once.
gp3 lets you provision IOPS/throughput independently of size; io2 Block Express is for the highest-performance, latency-sensitive databases.
Add ElastiCache or CloudFront to cache hot data — this lowers latency and reduces load on databases and origins.

scenarios.scenario: A fleet of Linux application servers across multiple AZs must all read and write the same set of files concurrently, and the storage must scale automatically as data grows.
scenarios.question: Which storage service fits?

options.label: An EBS volume attached to one instance
Amazon EFS mounted by all instances
An S3 bucket mounted as a block device

scenarios.explanation: Amazon EFS is elastic, multi-AZ shared file storage that many Linux instances can mount concurrently. A standard EBS volume attaches to a single instance; instance store is ephemeral and local.

scenarios.scenario: An unpredictable, bursty image-thumbnail job runs a few hundred times a day, each execution finishing in under a second. The team wants zero idle cost and no server management.
scenarios.question: Which compute option is the best fit?

options.label: A always-on EC2 Auto Scaling group
AWS Lambda triggered by the upload event

scenarios.explanation: Short, event-driven, spiky work with no idle cost is the ideal Lambda use case — it scales automatically and you pay only per invocation/duration. Always-on EC2/EKS would incur idle cost and management overhead.

quiz.question: Which EC2 instance family is best for a workload that holds a very large dataset entirely in memory?
quiz.explanation: Memory-optimized families (R, X) provide high RAM-to-vCPU ratios for in-memory databases and caches. Compute-optimized suits CPU-bound work; storage-optimized suits high local IOPS.

quiz.question: What is a key difference between Amazon EBS and Amazon EFS?
options: EBS is object storage; EFS is block storage
EBS attaches to a single instance (generally); EFS is shared file storage multiple instances can mount
EFS is only available in one AZ; EBS spans all AZs
quiz.answer: EBS attaches to a single instance (generally); EFS is shared file storage multiple instances can mount
quiz.explanation: EBS provides block storage for one instance (with limited Multi-Attach for io1/io2); EFS is elastic, multi-AZ NFS file storage many Linux instances can share.

quiz.question: Which service reduces database read latency by keeping frequently accessed data in memory?
quiz.explanation: ElastiCache (Redis/Memcached) stores hot data in memory, cutting read latency and offloading the database.

quiz.question: Why might you choose the gp3 EBS volume type?
options: It is object storage for static websites
It lets you provision IOPS and throughput independently of volume size
It is ephemeral and lost on stop
It is only for Windows file shares
quiz.answer: It lets you provision IOPS and throughput independently of volume size
quiz.explanation: gp3 decouples performance from capacity — you can dial IOPS/throughput up without growing the volume, often at lower cost than gp2.
